## Course Description

This graduate-level course introduces the theory and application of causal inference in the context of biostatistics and epidemiology. Students will gain practical skills in using Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), estimating causal effects from observational data, and applying contemporary methods like propensity scores, instrumental variables, mediation analysis, and marginal structural models.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of the course, students will be able to:

1. Formulate causal questions using the potential outcomes framework.
2. Identify confounding and bias using causal diagrams (DAGs).
3. Apply causal effect estimation methods: G-formula, propensity scores, IVs.
4. Perform causal mediation analysis (NDE/NIE) with assumptions.
5. Implement marginal structural models for time-varying treatments.
6. Conduct sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding.
7. Reframe observational questions using target trial emulation.

## Prerequisite

A prior course in regression modeling is required. Familiarity with R is expected. If unsure, contact the instructor.

## Primary Texts

- **Hernán & Robins (HR)**: *Causal Inference: What If*  
  [https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/miguel-hernan/causal-inference-book](https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/miguel-hernan/causal-inference-book)  
- **Neal (2020)**: *Introduction to Causal Inference*  
  [https://www.bradyneal.com/causal-inference-course](https://www.bradyneal.com/causal-inference-course)

## Supplementary Texts

- Pearl, Glymour, Jewell: *Causal Inference in Statistics: A Primer*  
- Imbens & Rubin: *Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences*  
- VanderWeele: *Explanation in Causal Inference*  
- Brumback: *Fundamentals of Causal Inference with R*

## Software and Tools

- R, RStudio or VS Code + Quarto
- Key packages: `dagitty`, `MatchIt`, `WeightIt`, `cobalt`, `ivreg`, `mediation`

## Part I: Foundations of Causal Inference

| Week  | Dates      | Core Topic                   | Primary Readings                    | Optional Reading (Cunningham)  | Project Connection                                            |
| :---- | :--------- | :--------------------------- | :---------------------------------- | :----------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **1** | Aug 19, 21 | What is a Causal Effect?     | **HR:** Ch. 1-2 ; **Neal:** Ch. 1-2 | Ch. 2: Potential Outcomes      | Framing your research interest as a precise causal question.  |
| **2** | Aug 26, 28 | Causal Diagrams (DAGs)       | **Neal:** Ch. 3 ; **HR:** Ch. 6     | Ch. 3: Directed Acyclic Graphs | **Action:** Draw a preliminary DAG for your project idea.     |
| **3** | Sep 2, 4   | Confounding & Identification | **HR:** Ch. 7 ; **Neal:** Ch. 4     | Ch. 4: Regression              | Refining your project's DAG and identifying key confounders.  |
| **4** | Sep 9, 11  | Selection & Measurement Bias | **HR:** Ch. 8-9                     | \-                             | Considering potential sources of bias in your chosen dataset. |

## Part II: Methods for Estimating Causal Effects

| Week  | Dates         | Core Topic                  | Primary Readings                                    | Optional Reading (Cunningham)       | Project Connection                                                |
| :---- | :------------ | :-------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **5** | Sep 16, 18    | Modeling for Adjustment     | **HR:** Ch. 12, 13, 15 ; **Neal:** Ch. 7.2, 7.5-7.6 | Ch. 5: Matching & Subclassification | Deciding on a primary adjustment strategy for your project.       |
| **6** | Sep 23, 25    | Instrumental Variables (IV) | **HR:** Ch. 16 ; **Neal:** Ch. 9                    | Ch. 8: Instrumental Variables       | Does your research area have any plausible "natural experiments"? |
| **7** | Sep 30, Oct 2 | Effect Modification         | **HR:** Ch. 4-5                                     | \-                                  | Thinking about important subgroups for your project analysis.     |
| **8** | Oct 7         | Mediation I: Foundations    | **VanderWeele:** Ch. 1-2 ; **Neal:** Ch. 14         | \-                                  | Refining your DAG to include potential mediators.                 |
